records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — The public embed snippet concatenates `discourseUrl` without normalizing a trailing slash, so a normal origin value such as `https://forum.example.com` produces an invalid `/embed/best` URL and breaks the integration.
records.rationale: The diff shows `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` with no trailing-slash normalization. If embedders set `discourseUrl` to a bare origin like `https://forum.example.com` (the natural value, matching `Discourse.base_url` conventions), the concatenated string becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best...`, a malformed URL that breaks the embed. The mechanism is verifiable directly from the added line; whether documentation elsewhere mandates a trailing slash cannot be confirmed from the diff, so confidence is moderate.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every concurrent cache miss enqueues a retrieval job before deduplication occurs inside the worker, allowing a traffic burst to flood the shared job queue.
records.rationale: Verified from the diff: EmbedController#best calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) for every request with no known topic_id, and deduplication (the Redis setnx throttle in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?) plus the TopicEmbed.exists? check in perform_retrieve all run only after the job is dequeued. So a burst of cache misses can enqueue many redundant jobs before any dedup occurs. This is a real, specific concurrency/scalability concern introduced by this diff, not a correctness defect, so it qualifies as important_non_bug.

The embed views then render it unsanitized via '<%= raw post.cooked %>'. A compromised or malicious RSS feed therefore injects arbitrary HTML/script shown to visitors. This is a real security defect

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Defaulting cook_method to 1 selects raw_html for every ordinary post and enables site-wide stored XSS by bypassing the normal cooker.
records.rationale: The finding's core mechanism is false. `Post.cook_methods` is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` (app/models/post.rb in the diff), and Discourse's Enum assigns the first value 1, so `:regular = 1` and `:raw_html = 2`. The migration's `default: 1` therefore defaults ordinary posts to the regular cooking pipeline, not raw HTML; the raw-HTML bypass in `cook` (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`) only triggers on value 2, which is only set explicitly by PostCreator via the `cook_method` opt. There is no site-wide stored XSS introduced by this default.
records.stripped_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Defaulting cook_method to 1 selects raw_html for every ordinary post and enables site-wide stored XSS by bypassing the normal cooker.
